components.description: Linked character, Unicode identifier, and index in the searchable rail.
components.css: .ds-glyph{display:grid;grid-template-columns:26px 1fr 24px;align-items:center;gap:4px;width:210px;min-height:34px;padding:4px 7px;border:1px solid #dbc57e;border-radius:4px;background:#f7e8af;color:#3b3216;text-align:left;cursor:pointer}.ds-glyph>span{text-align:center;font:17px/1 "Public Sans Variable",sans-serif}.ds-glyph code{font:12px ui-monospace,Consolas,monospace}.ds-glyph small{color:var(--muted,#64675e);font:12px "Public Sans Variable",sans-serif;text-align:right}.ds-glyph:hover{border-color:#a4821e}.ds-glyph:active{background:#e3e2d7}.ds-glyph:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--focus,#775800);outline-offset:3px}

narrative.overview:
The interface is a light technical editor whose visual weight belongs to the bitmap content. Warm neutral panels keep controls legible while a dark atlas reveals transparency and letter edges. Yellow connects primary export actions with the current selection rather than competing with the font being edited.

The system is flat, compact, and precise. A single sans-serif family carries interface text; measured values and Unicode identifiers use a restrained monospace voice. Native controls and immediate linked previews make editing feel direct.
keyCharacteristics: Warm light surfaces with a dark pixel-inspection ground.
Restrained yellow action and selection emphasis.
Aligned measurements, native fields, and visible keyboard focus.

rules.name: The Linked Selection Rule
rules.body: Use the established yellow family to connect the active font, glyph row, and atlas bounds; keep unrelated controls neutral.

rules.name: The Content First Rule
rules.body: Let imported bitmap letters be the expressive typography; keep interface labels in the quiet sans-serif family.

rules.name: The Flat Workbench Rule
rules.body: Prefer borders and tonal grouping to decorative elevation so the imported font remains the visual focus.

dos: Do use the yellow family for primary actions and linked selection states.
Do retain native field behavior, visible focus, and the searchable alternative to atlas clicking.
Do preserve pixel-exact atlas inspection, offer Smooth and Pixel exact text previews, and keep overflow inside inspection surfaces.
Do use warm surfaces and hairline rules to group dense editing controls.
donts: Don't turn the editor into a decorative game-themed dashboard.
Don't replace the imported font's visual character with expressive interface typography.
Don't add motion that interrupts repeated editing or ignores reduced-motion preference.
Don't hide an essential editing action behind dragging alone.
